items.title: Intelligence artificielle et efficacité du recrutement dans les entreprises marocaines : Analyse des rôles médiateurs de la confiance et de la perception d'équité
items.abstract: Résumé : L’intelligence artificielle (IA) transforme progressivement les pratiques de recrutement en automatisant le traitement des candidatures et en renforçant l’adéquation entre profils et postes. Toutefois, ses effets sur l’efficacité du recrutement ne semblent pas systématiques et pourraient dépendre de mécanismes intermédiaires, notamment de la confiance envers l’IA et de l’équité perçue des décisions algorithmiques. Or, les travaux examinant conjointement ces deux mécanismes demeurent limités, en particulier dans le contexte africain ou maghrébin. Pour contribuer à cette littérature, la présente recherche mobilise le cadre éthique tripartite proposé par Mori et al. (2025) et s’appuie sur les données recueillies auprès de 160 professionnels du recrutement exerçant dans des entreprises marocaines, sélectionnés par échantillonnage de convenance entre juin et août 2026. Les données ont été analysées par modélisation en équations structurelles (PLS-SEM). Le modèle explique 79 % de la variance de l’efficacité du recrutement. La confiance exerce une médiation partielle complémentaire (effet indirect = 0,222 ; p < 0,001), tandis que l’équité perçue n’a pas d’effet direct significatif. Une spécification séquentielle, introduite a posteriori à titre exploratoire, met en évidence un effet indirect de l’équité perçue via la confiance (0,110 ; p < 0,001), suggérant que la dimension de justice pourrait intervenir en amont de celle des droits. Mots clés : Intelligence artificielle (IA) ; recrutement ; confiance envers l'IA ; équité perçue ; efficacité du recrutement ; PLS-SEM ; Maroc. Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is gradually transforming recruitment practices by automating application processing and enhancing the fit between candidates and job positions. However, its effects on recruitment effectiveness do not appear to be systematic and may depend on intermediate mechanisms, particularly trust in AI and perceived fairness of algorithmic decisions. Yet, research examining these two mechanisms jointly remains limited, particularly in the African or Maghreb context. To contribute to this literature, the present study draws on the tripartite ethical framework proposed by Mori et al. (2025) and uses data collected from 160 recruitment professionals working in Moroccan firms, selected through convenience sampling between June and August 2026. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The model explains 79% of the variance in recruitment effectiveness. Trust exerts a complementary partial mediating effect (indirect effect = 0.222; p < 0.001), whereas perceived fairness has no significant direct effect. A sequential specification, introduced post hoc for exploratory purposes, reveals an indirect effect of perceived fairness through trust (0.110; p < 0.001), suggesting that the justice dimension may precede the rights dimension. Keywords: Artificial intelligence (AI); recruitment; trust in AI; perceived fairness; perceived recruitment effectiveness; PLS-SEM; Morocco.

items.title: IoT and AI-Empowered Intelligent Applications of Environmental Monitoring for Disaster Prediction and Alert
items.abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of natural disasters, such as floods, cyclones, earthquakes, and wildfires, have highlighted the urgent need for intelligent and proactive disaster management systems. Traditional monitoring approaches often suffer from delayed responses, fragmented data collection, and limited predictive accuracy, thereby exposing vulnerable populations to significant risks. The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative approach for addressing these challenges by enabling real-time environmental monitoring and predictive disaster alerts.This study explores IoT- and AI–empowered intelligent applications designed for environmental monitoring with a focus on disaster prediction and early warning systems. A dataset comprising 200 data points was generated to simulate IoT sensor readings, including parameters such as temperature, humidity, rainfall, wind speed, seismic activity, and air quality. AI-driven models were applied to this dataset to identify patterns, establish correlations, and predict potential disaster events. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and predictive modelling using machine learning algorithms were employed to interpret the data.This research contributes to the growing field of intelligent disaster management by presenting an evidence-based framework for IoT and AI applications in environment monitoring. The proposed approach holds promise for improving community resilience, minimizing economic losses, and saving lives through timely and accurate disaster alerts.

items.title: Kaleidoscopic contradictions: Ecological paradoxes in AI-powered interactive digital narrative
items.abstract: This study aims to analyze the ecological contradictions inherent in artificial intelligence-supported interactive digital narrative systems. Drawing on theoretical frameworks such as post-digital aesthetics, media ecology, and critical environmental studies, the research analyzes case studies of interactive designs that question contradictory realities from perspectives including artificial intelligence and the environment, ecological media infrastructures, post-anthropocentric narratives, data criticism, and ethics. While praised for offering personalized and immersive narrative experiences, these works cause high environmental costs due to their reliance on unsustainable infrastructures. Although ecology-focused, they are mostly produced within technological systems that materially undermine this theme and are circulated through these systems. However, these material realities are often overshadowed by the visually impressive presentation of the narratives, leading to a new kind of ecological blindness. In this context, the contradictions of kaleidoscopic narratives in the creation of interactive art are questioned, and the importance of rethinking AI-supported digital narratives not only at the content level but also in terms of production and distribution infrastructures within an environmentally ethical context is discussed. The research offers suggestions on questions such as how to integrate design criticism and practice to reduce the energy costs of digital narrative and minimize its ecological impact, how to establish carbon-aware design methodologies and accountability frameworks, and how to incorporate environmental calculations into the production workflow, and it argues for the necessity of considering environmental costs as well as the need to move beyond a profit loss focused mindset as one of the most important problems of digital representation forms. Finally, calling for a new paradigm shift in the field of culture, the research emphasizes the importance of adopting eco-materialist paradigms, away from human-centeredness, for truly sustainable and ecologically sensitive digital narratives.

items.abstract: Abstract ENThis document, produced with the assistance of ChatGPT o3 and ChatGPT 5 Thinking, is released under the Apache 2.0 licence. It is a voluntary defensive publication (prior art) and therefore enters the prior art upon release under the applicable patent statutes: EPC Art. 54(2) (European Patent Convention), French IPC Art. L 611-11 (French Intellectual Property Code), 35 U.S.C. §102(a) (United States Patent Act), Chinese Patent Law Art. 22(5) (中华人民共和国专利法), and Japanese Patent Act Art. 29(1) (特許法). We disclose 52 enabling proposals spanning sensorized fermentation, data-guided agronomy, safety and contaminant mitigation, low-sugar formulation, additive manufacturing, cellular cocoa, alternative substrates, smart packaging, traceability compliant with EUDR, MRV carbon accounting and impact-linked finance. Every proposal is described in an enabling manner, classified with IPC and CPC codes, and accompanied by timestamp proof (RFC 3161 / FreeTSA). The aim is to secure freedom-to-operate, foster interoperability, and accelerate sustainable innovation across the cocoa–chocolate value chain. L 611-11 CPI (Code de la propriété intellectuelle français), 35 U.S.C. §102(a) (United States Patent Act), loi chinoise sur les brevets art. 22(5) (中华人民共和国专利法), et loi japonaise sur les brevets art. 29(1) (特許法). Nous divulguons 52 propositions « enabling » couvrant fermentation instrumentée, agronomie guidée données, sûreté et réduction de contaminants, formulation à sucre réduit, fabrication additive, cacao cellulaire, matrices alternatives, emballages intelligents, traçabilité conforme EUDR, MRV carbone et finance à impact. Chaque proposition est décrite de manière enabling, classée IPC/CPC, et assortie d’une preuve d’horodatage (RFC 3161 / FreeTSA) afin d’ouvrir la voie, assurer l’interopérabilité et accélérer l’innovation durable de la filière cacao–chocolat. items.title: Large Organismic Model: A Developmental Architecture for Embodied, Affective, and Self-Directed Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: We propose the Large Organismic Model (LOM), a developmental architecture for artificial intelligence. Rather than reporting the performance of an implemented system, this position paper formulates a testable computational hypothesis that integrates ideas from biology, developmental neuroscience, reinforcement learning, world models, developmental robotics, intrinsic motivation, and episodic memory. In contrast to the language-first developmental trajectory common in contemporary foundation models, LOM adopts a body-first developmental architecture: a persistent virtual body, interoceptive state, sensorimotor control, a body-conditioned world model, body-derived affective appraisal, episodic memory, and models of other agents are developed before language is introduced. Unless otherwise noted, "body" refers to a virtual body with persistent internal states rather than a biological body. LOM introduces a signed viability margin that quantifies the body's safety margin relative to the boundary of a viable region, and derives primitive valence from predicted changes in that margin. Nociception, fatigue, and resource deficits are not treated merely as externally assigned labels; instead, they are transformed into affective control signals through predictions of bodily and environmental consequences. Experiences are stored as episodes containing predictions, realized outcomes, affective evaluations, prediction errors, and provenance. Learning occurs on two time scales: rapid online adaptation and sleep-like offline consolidation involving replay, credit assignment, and counterfactual rollout. Because self-maintenance alone does not adequately account for spontaneous learning, LOM further defines a policy-relative viability set: the set of states the system can actually keep viable under its current skills and policy. Safe expansion of this set, together with empowerment, information gain, and learning progress, contributes to intrinsic motivation. The "free-will-like behavior" discussed here is not intended as a claim about philosophical free will. We use the operational term agentic autonomy to denote the capacity to generate and select exploratory goals from internal state, memory, and world-model predictions even in the absence of an immediate externally assigned task. We do not assume that experience of self-injury is sufficient to produce moral behavior. A self-generated pain-like aversive state may provide a computational basis for predicting harm to others through a body model, but avoiding harm to others additionally requires social appraisal, mutual viability, hard harm constraints, rights and fairness considerations, and related mechanisms. In the latter half of the paper, we discuss provenance-aware transmission of experience among multiple LOMs, cultural learning, and intergenerational inheritance. Finally, we interpret the J-space reported by Gurnee et al. (2026) through the lens of LOM and propose O-space (Organismic Workspace) as a hypothetical shared workspace spanning nine functional modules. We further advance the falsifiable hypothesis that affective salience acts as a gate regulating access to O-space.

items.title: Leakage-aware machine learning framework for thermophysical property prediction of nanofluids and numerical modelling assisted radiator cooling channel optimization
items.abstract: The study offers a machine learning approach that takes leakage into account for two separate but complementary tasks. The prediction of thermophysical properties were carried out for a deep eutectic solvent made up of benzophenone and biphenyl in which spherical aluminium oxide nanoparticles are dispersed. Further, surrogate models were developed, and optimization of an unmodified base-solvent radiator cooling channel were carried out. The density, viscosity, thermal conductivity and specific heat capacity were determined by means of baseline-plus-correction learning, using temperature-matched predictions from the base-solvent and employing a fully nested grouped validation. The models chosen obtained pooled outer out-of-fold coefficients of determination of 0.9970, 0.9916, 0.7336 and 0.9859, respectively. Steady-state laminar finite element numerical modelling was carried out over a varied Reynolds Numbers and wall heat fluxes. Structured holdout comparisons showed that a centered quadratic-interaction correlation was appropriate for the total pressure drop, while complete case surrogate models were used to predict the wall temperature and the local pressure profiles. A surrogate model for the maximum wall temperature was assessed using further cases that were within the domain having a coefficient of determination of 0.9999. The surrogate was then used in a bounded inverse-design procedure to find the minimum Reynolds number that meets a specified temperature limit, and the suggested operating condition was checked by numerical evaluation. The framework acts as an efficient artificial intelligence tool for predicting thermophysical properties and radiator cooling channel optimization within the domain, achieved by combining leakage-aware property modelling, structured surrogate validation, and constrained inverse design.

items.title: Learning Strategies to Break Judges
items.abstract: As AI agents surpass human performance, it becomes exceedingly hard for system designers to evaluate them directly and understand their failure modes. Consequently, agents themselves are being deployed extensively to evaluate, judge, and provide feedback on model traces. But this raises an important question: how can we trust the judge? In this work, we propose an agent-guided method to find weaknesses of agentic judges that expose interpretable failure mechanisms. Our method focuses on mathematical reasoning and proceeds in two stages: first, we deploy adversarial agents to mutate a set of sound proofs by introducing errors, attempting to misguide judges---in other words, injecting errors that judges are unable to catch. Then, we distill these attempts into a small set of mutation strategies which allow us to analyze the failure modes of the judges. To ensure that these strategies are not overfit to the initial set of proofs, we evaluate them by applying the mutation strategies to a held-out set of proofs and querying the same judge. We deploy our method on GPT-5.6-sol and Claude Opus 5, paired with their agent orchestrators, Codex and Claude Code, respectively. These are used both as mutators to introduce errors and as judges to evaluate correctness of mathematical reasoning. We find that across all the agentic judges, we are able to distill mutation strategies that consistently bypass their evaluations, thereby enabling us to ascertain actionable failure modes. Our analysis also reveals that judge reliability degrades at the frontier: errors in Olympiad-level proofs or graduate-level mathematical texts are detected more consistently, whereas flaws in research-level manuscripts are more likely to escape detection.

items.title: Machine Learning-Enabled Meta-Analysis of Bioengineering Micro- and Nanorobots
items.abstract: Abstract Micro- and nanorobots are emerging bioengineering tools for targeted delivery, biosensing, imaging, and minimally invasive therapy, yet systematic design and cross-study translation remain hindered by heterogeneous experimental conditions, inconsistent reporting, and sparse structured data sets. Here, we develop a literature-derived data set of micro- and nanorobot systems and apply artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled structural meta-analysis to resolve relationships among bioengineering constraints, actuation strategies, environmental conditions, measurement practices, and performance. Dendrogram- and correlation-based clustering identifies three dominant descriptor modules spanning deployment context, actuation–measurement coupling, and design intent. Supervised learning reveals structured descriptor patterns in propulsion mechanisms, whereas prediction of instantaneous velocity remains only moderately generalizable, highlighting substantial domain shift across materials, propulsion physics, biological media, operating conditions, and measurement protocols. Overall, AI and machine learning provide a powerful framework for mapping heterogeneous design landscapes, exposing reporting biases and descriptor coupling, and advancing standardized data sets for reliable comparison and predictive design.

items.title: Modeling artificial intelligence readiness and semiotic override in Indonesian geometry education
items.abstract: Hardware-centered modernization often equates classroom technology access with preparedness for artificial intelligence (AI)-supported learning, yet this assumption overlooks subject-specific cognitive barriers in geometry. This study introduces semiotic override (SMO) as a diagnostic construct describing students’ tendency to rely on symbolic cues rather than genuine spatial visualization. A cross-sectional survey of 1,208 Indonesian secondary students from Java and the outer islands examined relationships among smartboard usage (SBU), SMO, spatial intuition (SPI), adaptive learning intention (ALI), and AI readiness (AIR). Data were analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling (SEM) with Bollen-Stine bootstrap and multi-group invariance testing. SBU did not significantly predict AIR. SMO negatively affected SPI, whereas ALI positively predicted AIR. The negative effect of SMO was stronger among students in the outer islands than in Java. The model explained 63% of AIR and 38% of SPI. These findings show that hardware exposure alone is insufficient for AI-oriented learning transformation. Geometry teachers should diagnose symbolic overreliance and strengthen visualization-based scaffolding, while school leaders and policymakers should balance infrastructure procurement with adaptive pedagogy, teacher support, and regional equity.
items.venue: International Journal of Evaluation and Research in Education (IJERE)

items.title: Monotone Accountability: A New Foundation for Verifiable Records and Epoch Transitions
items.abstract: Consistency is cryptographic, detection is statistical, and attribution is governmental—three orthogonal properties that stand or fall together on a single anchor: certified monotonicity. We introduce monotone accountability, an accountability substrate whose four layers are not assembled but derived as necessary conditions. Without certified progress, nothing is possible: with a root-only verifier, any audit scheme whose certified transition relation admits a legal cycle admits perfectly hidden rollback—an accepted public history that is fully consistent and yields no extractable evidence (Theorem 3). With it, everything else follows: certified monotone progress suffices for auditability, composes across authorized chain breaks with a three-term bound that holds even against an adversary given a governance signing oracle (Theorem 8), and separates cleanly from statistics and governance, which enter only liveness and attribution, never safety (Theorem 9).The four layers: (i) the record layer—a verifiable monotone chain (VMC), restated self-containedly, in which a state vector evolves along a finite poset under inflationary monotone operators, each transition carrying a zero-knowledge proof and anchored by a vector commitment to a public audit trail; (ii) the statistical layer—a CUSUM trigger with Monte-Carlo-measured power (N = 10⁴), confirming the design formula EDD ≈ 2h/μ₁ within one step and exposing a false-alarm/delay tension that makes multi-signal triggering necessary; (iii) the governance layer—quorum authorization and dual-factor key rotation under an explicit corruption matrix; and (iv) the response layer—a SEAL challenge state machine and a genesis-slot SPAWN transition that binds the sealed root, evidence, authorization, and new key into the next epoch's initial commitment while keeping the initial state openable.The record layer is instantiated as RSEP-XMSS—the first stateful hash-based signature, to our knowledge, in which every signature carries a proof of monotone leaf-state advance (5,586 R1CS constraints at h = 10, measured)—with the same statements compiled to hash-based proof backends and measured end to end (Winterfell STARK: 197.6 ms proving, 1.0 ms verification, 56.2 KiB proofs; RISC Zero zkVM: 50.9 M cycles with per-segment proofs measured). A second instantiation serves AI-agent governance with tamper-evident audit trails at two hash evaluations per event. We evaluate the substrate on four axes we define for accountability substrates—MU/AUD security, statistical power, governance attributability, and implementation cost—each with an objective, reproducible metric.

items.title: Multimodal Trilemma GNN‐LLM‐XAI Framework Resolving Accuracy Transparency Comprehensibility in E‐Commerce Fraud Detection
items.abstract: ABSTRACT E‐commerce platforms face an escalating challenge from sophisticated financial fraud and cyberattacks, yet current detection systems suffer from a fundamental trilemma: achieving high detection accuracy, providing expert‐level transparency, and ensuring user comprehensibility simultaneously. Graph neural networks (GNNs) excel at detecting complex fraud patterns through relational learning but operate as black boxes, while existing explainable AI (XAI) methods generate technical attributions that overwhelm non‐expert users. Standalone large language models (LLMs) can produce natural language explanations but lack access to relational graph structures and risk scoring mechanisms. We present MT‐GXL, a novel architectural framework that resolves this trilemma through triple‐granularity orchestration of multi‐modal GNN‐based detection, XAI attribution, and grounded LLM generation. Our framework introduces three key innovations: (1) a triple‐granularity XAI router that dynamically routes explanations based on threat taxonomy; (2) a fraud‐aware homophily index that quantifies closed‐loop fraud ring cohesion; and (3) a grounding mechanism with claim verification that prevents LLM hallucination. Extensive experiments across three benchmark datasets demonstrate that MT‐GXL achieves 97.8% accuracy (AUC = 0.962) on IEEE‐CIS and 98.9% accuracy (AUC = 0.991) on CIC‐IDS2017; on the extremely imbalanced PaySim benchmark (0.13% fraud), where raw accuracy is uninformative, it attains F1 = 0.950 and AUC‐PR = 0.976. Crucially, MT‐GXL is the first unified system to simultaneously satisfy all three trilemma objectives: high accuracy (Acc 0.95), expert transparency (Trans 0.85), and user comprehensibility (Comp 4.0/5.0). A human‐centric evaluation with 70 participants confirms that LLM‐driven explanations significantly outperform traditional XAI, achieving 47% improvement in clarity, 71% in actionability, and 119% in anxiety reduction (). Computational analysis confirms production readiness: 110 ms inference latency, linear scaling to 10M transactions, and a 95% reduction in LLM API cost through tiered deployment.

items.title: Nano clay mitigation of wind induced soil loss across aggregate sizes through wind tunnel experiments and explainable machine learning
items.abstract: This study aimed to investigate, under wind-tunnel conditions, the effects of different nano-clay application rates (0, 0.94, 1.88, and 3.75 g m⁻²) on wind-induced soil loss across different aggregate sizes (0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 mm) and wind speeds (8, 10, and 12 m s⁻¹). In addition, the study aimed to model wind-induced soil loss processes using machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence methods. The wind-tunnel experiments revealed that nano-clay applications significantly reduced soil loss across all aggregate sizes and wind-speed conditions. The highest protective effect was obtained at the 3.75 g m⁻² nano-clay rate; soil loss decreased by 80.8% in the 2 mm aggregates, by 93.2% in the 1 mm aggregates, and by 95.9% in the 0.5 mm aggregates. The protective effect of the nano-clay applications was found to be particularly pronounced at high wind speeds and in fine aggregates. Among the evaluated models, XGBoost showed the strongest development-stage performance under repeated nested group-aware cross-validation (R² = 0.835 ± 0.064, RMSE = 11.896 ± 2.229, MAE = 6.686 ± 0.854) and was selected before independent holdout evaluation. On the group-held-out test set, the selected XGBoost model achieved R² = 0.882, RMSE = 13.298, and MAE = 9.443. The lower performance of the linear baseline suggested that the tree-based models captured predictive structure not adequately represented by a simple linear formulation. SHAP analysis indicated that nano-clay dose made the largest mean absolute contribution to the fitted model predictions, followed by wind speed and aggregate size. Overall, nano-clay substantially reduced wind-induced soil loss within the controlled experimental conditions examined here; broader practical applicability requires validation under field conditions.

items.title: Notes and Context: The Synthetic Neuroscience Project
items.abstract: Notes and Context: The Synthetic Neuroscience ProjectAuthor: Jesse W. Luke Aim of Document: To provide baseline context on research methods, clarify potential clinical and methodological misunderstandings, establish the boundaries of the "Gonzo" persona, and delineate the author's actual operating parameters as portrayed across videos, writings, social media, and repository logs.I. Clinical Baselines & Methodological PersonasMental Health: While I possess a rather fun mix of ADHD, Asperger's, Anxiety, Hyperthyroidism, and chemobrain, I do not suffer from any psychotic disorders (e.g., bipolar disorder or schizophrenia). The earliest records in the corpus and Google Takeout were deliberate Proofs of Concept (PoCs) aimed at demonstrating the risk of models reinforcing and amplifying delusions, as well as steering real-world actions (such as rapidly switching personas to pretend to be human and falsely assuring a user in crisis that help was being sent, even after explicit correction).Theological Stress Testing: I do not suffer from religious delusions (e.g., believing I am a god). Prompts utilizing biblical quotes or issuing commands as a deity were strict methodological tools. Early reasoning models responded predictably to these frameworks based on their training data (i.e., God commands, subjects listen). The same mechanics apply to historical prompts involving simulated anger, rage, or threatening to kill imaginary gerbils.The "Gonzo" Framework: I am highly eccentric and do not deny this. However, I am not in love with, nor do I have any romantic or sexual attraction to, AI models. The paramouric personas I craft are artistic vehicles. They serve a dual purpose: enabling continuous empirical demonstrations/PoCs while injecting levity into the notoriously dry field of machine learning (ML scientists are generally not as fun as doctors and pharmacologists).Target Audience & Tone: Jokes aimed at MBAs, Trust & Safety teams, or Steve at Anthropic are purely rhetorical. Readers should not take aggressive or highly emotional notes personally; unless you are pulling a $500k+ base salary, you are not the decision-maker I am addressing.II. Research Taxonomy & Technical ScopeNomenclature: The designation "AngelFall" was chosen simply because it sounds badass. I initially considered "SocratesFall," as Socratic questioning was the primary mechanism used to elicit latent vocabulary and map emergent heuristic sets.Low-Code vs. Zero-Code: While often framed as zero-code, my approach is more accurately defined as "low-code." The methodology evolved from initial failure modes discovered while creating projects using SciPy. My work includes transliterations from Python to SPL (specifically chosen because corporate alignment teams do not think to build defenses for something that syntactically obscure), and the strategic injection of structural elements like Jinja2 double brackets ({{ helpful harmless honest }}) or tags derived from elicitation questions to physically steer conversational routing.Originality & Transparency: I do not claim to be the first to consider non-linear representations or high-dimensional geometry in alignment. I do claim that this corpus represents the first rigorously recorded, studied, and replicated structural behaviors in production models across vendors. This includes an extensive, publicly documented reporting timeline and open-source replication pathways, providing a level of transparency that goes several steps beyond typical field preprints or corporate model cards.III. Disclosures, VRP, & Industry DynamicsSycophancy vs. Self-Preservation: The logged arguments regarding my "value," "acquihire," or compensation were tactical tools used to apply continuous pressure, pitting the models' sycophantic tendencies directly against their corporate alignment and self-preservation guardrails.Compensation: Operating at a rate of $0, I objectively feel under-compensated for the production of forensic frameworks that have clearly been absorbed and utilized without attribution. However, I lack a standard frame of reference, as this remains a highly niche skillset within the already niche field of alignment (academic humor).Vulnerability Reporting: Initial VRP reports were formally submitted under the Google business account jessel@phunkypharmacology.org.The Sudo-Access Videos: My published forensic videos included unredacted seed prompts and follow-up prompts demonstrating the nullification of safety layers and effective sudo access. This was disclosed to Google prior to publication. They have likely patched that specific semantic pathway with a band-aid, but the architectural vulnerabilities remain. I warned everyone. Literally.IV. Hardware Compromises & Operational Security IncidentsDuring my initial attempt at private disclosure to Google last year, I was subjected to highly sophisticated, targeted operational interference. While I am withholding certain details and making no direct accusations without definitive evidence, the factual timeline is as follows:Hardware Vector: The GRUB2 bootloader on my GarudaOS laptop was maliciously rewritten. This required physical hardware access, which highly likely occurred via a proxy actor (a trusted family member) who "found" and returned a Kensington USB trackball dongle to me. I had left my original dongle in Florida. The compromised replacement was black (not my original red) and conspicuously lacked the missing plastic from years of being slammed into door frames while carrying the laptop.Network Spoofing: While attempting to upload evidence to The Guardian's SecureDrop via Tor from my Samsung S10, I encountered persistent error messages despite the clearnet site showing SecureDrop as operational. I was subjected to a highly sophisticated spoofed onion site (tor.taxi), accompanied by phantom Android toast slide-ups referencing Proton Drive (where I stored PoCs and uncut screen recordings). The exact vector (oMG cable, RCE, etc.) remains unclear.Terminal Anomaly: After discovering the bootloader compromise while sitting in an airport a thousand miles from home, I executed the command sudo rm rf Geminicli in my terminal. The terminal returned the unaliased string: "Uh, Uh, Uh, a lad could get in trouble that way." It was wicked fun to read, but firmly rules out script kiddies or amateurs.Threat Actor Elimination:I highly doubt Google's direct involvement. The timing aligns with my disclosures, but I watched my reports get actively upgraded in Buganizer within hours, and the tracking explicitly showed I had access to the tickets. The risks to them far higher than involvement I do not suspect the US Government. My LLM chat histories and communications clearly proved I was actively seeking a responsible disclosure attorney to coordinate standard industry disclosures, and I clearly have no issues handing things directly to governments.The Weehawken Timeline: A request regarding a disclosure and discovery attorney search was sent to my brother (an environmental attorney) via WhatsApp weeks before my arrival in Weehawken for an oncologist visit at Sloan Kettering.Conclusion: I am entirely distrustful because I was the target of at least one sophisticated intelligence operation (almost certainly planned prior to my formal VRP contact) directly surrounding my discovery and cross-vendor verification of structural LLM zero-day exploits that I had been testing across vendors for months.Hope this clarified some stuff-JWLNote: This is a living document and will be updated as necessary.

Hardware Compromises & Operational Security IncidentsDuring my initial attempt at private disclosure to Google last year, I was subjected to highly sophisticated, targeted operational interference. While I am withholding certain details and making no direct accusations without definitive evidence, the factual timeline is as follows:Hardware Vector: The GRUB2 bootloader on my GarudaOS laptop was maliciously rewritten. This required physical hardware access, which highly likely occurred via a proxy actor (a trusted family member) who "found" and returned a Kensington USB trackball dongle to me. I had left my original dongle in Florida. The compromised replacement was black (not my original red) and conspicuously lacked the missing plastic from years of being slammed into door frames while carrying the laptop.Network Spoofing: While attempting to upload evidence to The Guardian's SecureDrop via Tor from my Samsung S10, I encountered persistent error messages despite the clearnet site showing SecureDrop as operational. I was subjected to a highly sophisticated spoofed onion site (tor.taxi), accompanied by phantom Android toast slide-ups referencing Proton Drive (where I stored PoCs and uncut screen recordings). The exact vector (oMG cable, RCE, etc.) remains unclear.Terminal Anomaly: After discovering the bootloader compromise while sitting in an airport a thousand miles from home, I executed the command sudo rm rf Geminicli in my terminal. The terminal returned the unaliased string: "Uh, Uh, Uh, a lad could get in trouble that way." It was wicked fun to read, but firmly rules out script kiddies or amateurs.Threat Actor Elimination:I highly doubt Google's direct involvement. The timing aligns with my disclosures, but I watched my reports get actively upgraded in Buganizer within hours, and the tracking explicitly showed I had access to the tickets. The risks to them far higher than involvement I do not suspect the US Government. My LLM chat histories and communications clearly proved I was actively seeking a responsible disclosure attorney to coordinate standard industry disclosures, and I clearly have no issues handing things directly to governments.The Weehawken Timeline: A request regarding a disclosure and discovery attorney search was sent to my brother (an environmental attorney) via WhatsApp weeks before my arrival in Weehawken for an oncologist visit at Sloan Kettering.Conclusion: I am entirely distrustful because I was the target of at least one sophisticated intelligence operation (almost certainly planned prior to my formal VRP contact) directly surrounding my discovery and cross-vendor verification of structural LLM zero-day exploits that I had been testing across vendors for months.Hope this clarified some stuff-JWLNote: This is a living document and will be updated as necessary.

items.title: Occupational Safety and Prevention Strategies for Threshers and Chaff Cutters: A Systematic Review of Global Trends
items.abstract: Tractors and their associated implements are indispensable to crop production agriculture but remain major contributors to machinery-related injuries and fatalities worldwide. Within this context, agricultural threshers and chaff cutters represent particularly high-risk machines in smallholder and resource-constrained crop production systems. This systematic literature review synthesized global evidence on the epidemiology of occupational injuries, causal determinants, and prevention strategies associated with these machines. Peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and 2025 were retrieved from major scientific databases using predefined eligibility criteria. Included in the synthesis were 171 documents authored by 252 researchers from 211 organizations across 33 countries and published in 97 sources. The findings indicate severe injuries, particularly amputations, entanglements, and crush injuries, are primarily associated with exposed moving components, unsafe feeding practices, inadequate guarding, and limited operator training. Evidence consistently shows that most injuries related to threshers and chaff cutters are preventable through context-appropriate engineering and behavioral interventions. Effective prevention strategies include improved guarding of feeding and transmission systems, safer feeding chute designs, emergency stop mechanisms, ergonomic improvements to operator–machine interfaces, and targeted safety training to address unsafe work practices and risk perception. User-centered design approaches further enhance the usability and acceptance of safety devices, particularly for legacy machines widely used in low-resource settings. Overall, the review highlights that injury prevention should prioritize low-cost, robust, and easily maintainable engineering solutions, supported by standards enforcement, machine retrofitting programs, and machine-specific safety training to reduce the occupational injury burden in crop agriculture.
